derivation:
1757. Exact elimination of the ORIGINAL fine fixed-exterior deltas in the full averaged-gauge Haar chart. This is a raw finite-group constrained-kernel operation, not a new norm lemma, a final Landau determinant, or an assertion that a source's already eliminated fluctuation variables are raw links.

INPUT DATA AND UNCHANGED LAW. Let E be one independent orientation per fine link of the SAME original finite torus, S its sites, and G the original compact matrix Lie group. U0 is the fixed original real/unitary background. F subset E is EXACTLY the original prescribed raw fine-link exterior set, with fixed data V0 in G^F. F is not replaced by a point-ring incident lift or an enlarged active domain. Keep the original chosen physical mean M_fix, coarse row set C_phys, original field domain D, original action, exponential gauge weights and other ordinary measurable density factors f(U;V,V0,J). The previously fixed coupling, beta_ref, g1_ref and cutoff law are not changed. This calculation does not newly identify the later free-algebra cutoff K_C(g0) with a raw-link domain; that dictionary remains required before applying it to the unfinished physical profile. Additional singular gauge constraints require their already admitted measure meaning; the proof below treats the explicit fine-link Dirac embedding and weak coarse pushforward, with all original ordinary factors retained.

On the same fine torus choose, ONLY IF COMPATIBLE, an auxiliary native anchored block partition with root set R and the source canonical comb forest T. Each nonroot has one parent in its own native block. Tree edges are oriented from parent to child for the recursion; if an independent representative in E has the other orientation, use the inverse of its prescribed value. No extra reversed-link variable is introduced. Let n=|S|, m=|E|, r0=|R|. Then |T|=n-r0. Put P_rz=U0(Gamma_rz). The full chart has k(r)=I, a_r(k)=exp[sum_z L^-d Log(Ad_P_rz k(z))], g_r=a_r(k)^-1, l_g(z)=P_rz^-1 g_r P_rz, u=l_g k, Y_e=U0_e on T, and U=Psi(Y,k)=Y^(u^-1). Every Log here is smooth and Lie(G)-valued on the admitted k chart C, not merely a defined matrix-log branch. All mean evaluations below are restricted to the actual pullback domain with its admitted covariant branch. No nonemptiness of this chart at the prescribed V0 is asserted.

First verify, rather than assume from a Jacobian label, the two facts used by the elimination. Along a tree edge e=(p,z), P_rz=P_rp U0_e, so l_g(p) U0_e l_g(z)^-1=U0_e. Therefore

 Psi_e=k(p)^-1 U0_e k(z),  e in T.

On a non-tree edge b, Psi_b=u(b_-)^-1 Y_b u(b_+). Standard rooted-tree coordinates U=Z^(k^-1) preserve full product Haar; at fixed k, Y=Z^(l_g) is an independent left/right translation of each non-tree Z_b and keeps the tree values. Hence dU=dY_(E\T) dk_(S\R) on the full chart. This is a full-coordinate Haar identity. No Lie-algebra exponential density, root quotient volume, final Faddeev-Popov factor or coarse-constraint pivot determinant is set equal to one.

STEP A: ELIMINATE ONLY THE PRESCRIBED TREE EDGES. Let T_F=T intersect F, with t=|T_F|. The graph (S,T_F) is a forest. Each component has a unique site closest to its native root; call it its top site. A component either contains its native root, or its top site is a nonroot. Let A be the set of top sites of components not containing a native root. Introduce independent residual variables kappa_s in G for s in A. Set k(r)=I at each native root and k(s)=kappa_s at every residual top site. For each edge (p,z) in T_F, recursively define

 k(z)=U0_e^-1 k(p) V0_e.

This defines EVERY nonroot k(z): a component containing a native root starts at I; any other component starts at its kappa. It defines a smooth explicit word K(kappa,V0_TF) on the original variables, without any averaging operation, implicit equation, physical-sector assumption or new data. The count is |A|=n-r0-t, because the forest T_F has n-t components and exactly r0 contain native roots.

For a parent-to-child prescribed tree edge,

 delta_G(Psi_e V0_e^-1)=delta_G(k(p)^-1 U0_e k(z) V0_e^-1).

At fixed parent, the equation has the unique solution above; left/right Haar translations give integral dk(z) delta_G(...)=1. Solve from the top of each component toward its leaves, or use the triangular change from its non-top k variables to the tree-edge values. With any integrable test function H (allowed to depend on all k and Y),

 integral dk_(S\R) product_(e in T_F) delta_G(Psi_e V0_e^-1) H(Y,k)
 = integral dkappa_A H(Y,K(kappa,V0_TF)).

The argument uses the usual finite-product fine-coordinate Dirac embedding; no unexplained product of dependent constraints is being asserted. A rigorous version follows by first treating the t prescribed tree-edge values as independent target coordinates, applying the Haar product change, and then fixing those target coordinates; the target map is a smooth group-triangular global coordinate map. If T_F is empty, K=kappa at all nonroots and no variable is removed. If T_F=T, k is fully determined by the original tree data V0 and there is no kappa integration.

STEP B: ELIMINATE THE REMAINING PRESCRIBED FINE LINKS. Set F_N=F\T and f_N=|F_N|. After Step A, u depends only on kappa and fixed V0_TF (and fixed U0), never on the free Y links. For every b in F_N, the unique fine constraint is

 Y_b=V0_b^u := u(b_-) V0_b u(b_+)^-1.

At fixed kappa, Haar in Y_b is preserved by the two translations, so integrating its single fine delta has factor one. Let eta_b be the remaining independent Y coordinates on E\(T union F). Define Y*=Y*(eta,kappa;V0) by

 Y*_e=U0_e on T;
 Y*_b=V0_b^u on F_N;
 Y*_b=eta_b on E\(T union F).

Let U*=Psi(Y*,K). Then U*_F=V0 exactly: Step A gives the prescribed tree edges and Step B gives all other prescribed links. Conversely every original U with U_F=V0 and k_U in C yields exactly one (eta,kappa): use the tree inverse k_U(z)=P_rz^-1 U(Gamma_rz), take its values at A, and its corresponding free Y links eta. Thus this is a complete chart on that fixed-fine-exterior subspace. The dimension count is

 |A| + |E\(T union F)| = (n-r0-t)+(m-(n-r0)-f_N)=m-|F|.

All independent original exterior constraints have been eliminated once. No selected coarse-mean pivot b0(c), no previous free-fluctuation coordinate and no source Landau equation has been eliminated a second time. Dependence of u on eliminated k variables is fully substituted through K; it introduces off-diagonal terms but not a new diagonal determinant. The chosen order is essential: eliminate the tree k variables before treating the independent non-tree Y link targets.

EXACT FIXED-FINE-DATA HAAR IDENTITY. For every fixed original V0, and any measurable absolutely integrable H on the original fine subspace, its chart part satisfies

 integral_(U_F=V0) dU_(E\F) 1_{k_U in C} H(U)
 = integral d kappa_A integral d eta_(E\(T union F)) 1_{K(kappa,V0_TF) in C} H(U*(eta,kappa;V0)).

The equality is of measures, not merely a formal determinant identity. The fixed-fine-data measure on the left is canonically the original product Haar of active raw links, with the original fine coordinates inserted as V0. This measure exists for EVERY fine target V0 because those fine coordinates were independent links; it does NOT prove existence of a conditional measure after also fixing the nonlinear coarse targets. The original domain D stays as 1_D(U*) or a restriction to U* in D, never as a substituted product box in eta or kappa. The chart indicator may select an empty set. Full integration also retains the unchanged original off-chart part; no probability or estimate for it is supplied.

OPERATIONAL COARSE KERNEL WITH FINE DATA FIXED. Define the original chart-part coarse measure by its weak pairing with any bounded test function phi on the ORIGINAL coarse target space:

 <K_C(.;V0,J),phi> = integral_(U_F=V0) dU_(E\F) 1_{k_U in C} 1_D(U)
       f(U;M_fix(U),V0,J) phi(M_fix(U)).

Here f needs its actual graph evaluation and integrability, not an ambient L1 equivalence class with unspecified traces. Applying the identity gives the SAME expression on (eta,kappa) with U*. Equivalently the original formal coarse deltas can be written, still only as a weak measure in V,

 K_C(V;V0,J) = integral d kappa d eta 1_{K in C} 1_D(U*) f(U*;V,V0,J)
       product_(c in C_phys) delta_G(M_fix(Y*)(c) [V^u(c)]^-1),

 V^u(c)=u(c_-) V(c) u(c_+)^-1,

using the actual endpoints, not assumed native roots. Physical point-gauge equivariance and the same covariant admitted branch give M_fix(U*)=u_-^-1 M_fix(Y*) u_+. This does not replace the mean by the old relative average. It sharpens the earlier joint (V,V0) interpretation only in the fine data V0, whose independent-link embedding is now explicitly eliminated; coarse targets remain weak, and any claimed fixed-V density/conditional integral still requires a separate admission.

EXTERIOR COARSE ROWS AND FULL WORDS. Let S_c be the full set of fine edges required by the ACTUAL chosen physical mean row c, including all its actual path families and their reversed edges. Only if S_c is contained in F and that mean is defined on these data does M_fix(U*)(c)=M_fix(V0)(c). Such a row has its original exterior coarse delta once; do not multiply a new copy, solve a fictitious independent equation, or create a separate normalizer. This statement does not certify S_c subset F for any actual row without examining its support. Rows with crossing supports remain complete nonlinear functions of the retained coordinates.

For a complete rooted closed word, Phi_r(U*)=u(r)^-1 Phi_r(Y*)u(r), and a matrix source J_r is conjugated to u(r)J_r u(r)^-1. Open words retain both endpoint factors. Entirely prescribed words evaluate to Phi(V0) once in their ORIGINAL matrix order; crossing words are never split. Finite polynomial complex sources are handled coefficientwise under the original integrability. The real/unitary Wilson action satisfies A(U*)=A(Y*); every other original factor keeps its actual pullback unless its own invariance has been established. Any normalized expression requires the SAME full original denominator, including the off-chart part, and an already proved nonzero value.

RELATION TO NATIVE BOUNDARY DATA AND REMAINING PHYSICAL OBLIGATION. This elimination gives the concrete transported fine data V0^u and constraints tying them to the fixed native tree values; they are not independent exterior parameters that can now be frozen. The spaces-paper (1.31) boundary functional uses its typed, multiscale Vprime data and transported finer paths. We do NOT identify all of those inputs with the raw fine set F, or replace its left correction by log of a coarse target. Each input path/row must be classified in the original source strata and mapped through U* before evaluating that functional. In particular a crossing input that is not in F cannot be called a fixed fine datum. Native-to-physical section, coarse constraint pivots, the final constrained/Landau determinant, regularity collars, P1 held issue, beta_ref/g1_ref amplitude correspondence, simultaneous component-absorption parameter chain, off-chart estimates, nonzero normalization, connected sums and history are NOT paid. The specific new step is the exact fine-exterior constraint elimination and its Haar factor one on this chart, with no law/mean/domain substitution. Falsifiers are an incorrect tree recursion or orientation, a missing residual component root, u depending on a supposedly free Y link, a nonunit group-coordinate Haar factor, a false fixed-target coarse conclusion, double elimination, or any loss of a full word, original cutoff, exterior constraint or off-chart term.
